scenario: 面试官问「你会用什么数据？」，你想直接跳到模型架构，觉得数据是次要问题。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'what data would you use?' and you want to jump to model architecture, treating data as secondary.
q: 为什么说「能训的模型被能收的数据框死」？数据来源约束了什么？
q_en: Why is 'the model you can train is bounded by the data you can collect' true, and what does data sourcing constrain?
why: 数据来源直接约束标签空间、目标函数、服务延迟和合规边界——收到的信号决定标签空间、标签空间决定目标函数、目标函数决定性能天花板。架构再好也补不了弱数据策略。
why_en: Data sourcing constrains label space, objective function, serving latency, and compliance, so weak data caps the ceiling and architecture cannot compensate.
options: 数据只影响准确率的高低，只要把模型架构调得足够好，就总能补上一套本来就弱的数据采集策略
现代大模型的参数量已经大到不再受数据约束，架构设计的好坏才是唯一决定性能的瓶颈
数据来源的差异只体现在存储成本和带宽开销上,只要把这些基础设施成本控制住,跟模型最终能学到什么能力完全无关
数据来源约束标签空间、目标函数、服务延迟和合规;信号→标签→目标→性能天花板,架构补不了弱数据
options_en: Data only affects how high accuracy is; as long as the model architecture is tuned well enough, it can always make up for a weak data-collection strategy.
Modern large models have grown so big that they're no longer data-bounded; architecture design is the sole bottleneck on performance.

Differences in data sourcing only show up in storage cost and bandwidth overhead — as long as that infrastructure cost is kept under control, it's completely unrelated to what capabilities the model ends up learning.
Data sourcing constrains label space, objective, serving latency, and compliance; signals → labels → objective → performance ceiling, and architecture can't fix weak data.
optionExplanations: 架构补不了弱数据——没收到的信号根本进不了标签空间，再好的模型也学不到不存在的东西。
大模型同样受训练数据质量与覆盖约束，「不受数据约束」是误解。
存储成本只是一小块，数据来源真正决定的是模型能学到什么、优化什么，控制基础设施花费解决不了这个问题。
对；数据是上游地基，信号决定标签、标签决定目标、目标决定天花板，一路向下约束。
optionExplanations_en: Architecture can't fix weak data — signals you never collected can't enter the label space, and no model learns what isn't there.
Large models are equally bounded by training-data quality and coverage; 'not data-bounded' is a misconception.
Storage cost is a small piece; data sourcing really decides what the model can learn and optimize — controlling infrastructure spend doesn't fix that.
Correct — data is the upstream foundation: signals fix labels, labels fix the objective, the objective fixes the ceiling, constraining all the way down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型能学习预测的所有可能标签的集合，由你实际收集到的信号决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The label space is the set of all labels the model can learn to predict, determined by the signals you actually collect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时优化的量化目标(如最大化点击、最小化误分)，由标签空间派生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The objective function is the quantified target optimized during training (e.g. maximize clicks), derived from the label space.

scenario: 为推荐系统选训练信号：可用被动行为(点击、停留、跳过)或主动反馈(打分、点赞、评论)。
scenario_en: Choosing training signals for a recommender: passive behavior (clicks, dwell, skips) or intentional feedback (ratings, likes, reviews).
q: 隐式信号 vs 显式信号，区别是什么？
q_en: Implicit vs explicit signals — what's the difference?
why: 隐式=被动行为数据(点击、停留、滚动深度、购买、跳过)，用户无意提供反馈；显式=有意反馈(星级评分、点赞点踩、评论、问卷)。区别在用户是否主动、有意地表达偏好。
why_en: Implicit is passive behavioral data (clicks, dwell, skips) the user doesn't intend as feedback, while explicit is intentional feedback (ratings, thumbs, reviews) the user deliberately gives.
options: 隐式指服务器端记录留存的访问日志、显式指客户端弹窗收集的填写内容，按数据物理存在哪台机器划分
隐式=被动行为数据(点击/停留/跳过、无意提供)；显式=有意反馈(评分/点赞/评论)
隐式指用连续数值表示的特征、显式指用离散类别表示的特征，按数据类型划分
隐式指系统早期版本采集的旧数据、显式指改版后新采集的数据，按采集时间先后划分
options_en: Implicit means access logs recorded and kept on the server, explicit means form input collected via a client-side popup — split by which machine physically stores the data.
Implicit = passive behavioral data (clicks/dwell/skips, unintended); explicit = intentional feedback (ratings/likes/reviews).
Implicit means features represented as continuous numbers, explicit means features represented as discrete categories — split by data type.
Implicit means old data collected under an earlier system version, explicit means new data collected after a redesign — split by collection time.
optionExplanations: 隐式/显式不是按存储位置分，服务器和客户端都可能记录隐式行为。
对；核心区别是用户有没有主动、有意地表达偏好，隐式无意、显式有意。
数值 vs 类别是特征类型，与信号是否出自主动反馈无关。
新旧不是划分依据，隐式和显式可以同时、持续地被采集。
optionExplanations_en: Implicit/explicit isn't split by storage; both server and client can log implicit behavior.
Correct — the core difference is whether the user deliberately expresses preference: implicit unintended, explicit intended.
Numeric vs categorical is feature type, unrelated to whether a signal comes from intentional feedback.
Old vs new isn't the criterion; implicit and explicit are collected concurrently and continuously.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户无意提供的被动行为数据：点击、停留时长、滚动深度、购买、跳过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An implicit signal is passive behavioral data the user doesn't intend as feedback: clicks, dwell time, scroll depth, purchases, skips.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户有意给出的反馈：星级评分、点赞/点踩、评论、问卷。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An explicit signal is deliberate feedback the user gives: star ratings, thumbs up/down, reviews, surveys.

tradeoff: 隐式(被动、体量大、无意表达) vs 显式(主动、稀疏、有意表达)
tradeoff_en: Implicit (passive, high volume, unintended) vs explicit (active, sparse, deliberate).

scenario: YouTube 上人人都在产生观看行为，但只有不到 1% 的观看会被打一个显式评分。
scenario_en: On YouTube everyone generates watch behavior, but under 1% of views ever get an explicit rating.
q: 隐式 vs 显式在「体量 vs 稀疏」这一维上如何取舍？
q_en: On the volume-vs-sparsity axis, how do implicit and explicit signals trade off?
why: 隐式=覆盖：人人产生，体量大但每条模糊；显式=精度：<1% 才有评分，稀疏但每条清晰。隐式给覆盖广度、显式给单条准度，二者互补而非替代。
why_en: Implicit gives coverage (everyone generates it, but each is ambiguous) while explicit gives precision (under 1% rate, but each is clear), so they complement rather than replace each other.
tradeoff: 隐式(体量大、覆盖广、每条模糊) vs 显式(稀疏、覆盖窄、每条清晰)
options: 隐式=覆盖(人人产生、体量大),显式=精度(<1%评分、稀疏但清晰),互补不替代
隐式行为既多又准，显式评分又少又质量差，工程上应该完全弃用显式信号
两者的体量其实差不多,只是显式信号需要用户多点开一个评分入口、流程比隐式稍慢一点而已
显式信号因为含义清晰，所以体量也一定比隐式更大、覆盖用户也更全面
options_en: Implicit = coverage (everyone generates it, high volume), explicit = precision (<1% rated, sparse but clear); complementary, not substitutes.
Implicit behavior is both plentiful and accurate, while explicit ratings are scarce and low quality, so engineering should drop explicit signals entirely.
The two actually have similar volume; explicit signals just need the user to open one extra rating affordance, making the process a bit slower than implicit.
Because explicit signals are unambiguous, their volume must also be larger than implicit's, with fuller user coverage.
optionExplanations: 对;隐式给覆盖、显式给精度,<1%的评分率决定了显式只能做校准不能单撑。
隐式虽多但每条模糊，弃用显式就丢掉了校准隐式噪声的清晰锚点。
两者体量差一个数量级以上(<1% vs 近100%),多一步交互不是体量相近的原因,说「差不多」与事实不符。
清晰不代表体量大,显式恰恰因为要用户主动给而极其稀疏。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — implicit gives coverage, explicit gives precision, and the <1% rating rate means explicit can only calibrate, not stand alone.
Implicit is plentiful but each is ambiguous; dropping explicit loses the clear anchor that calibrates implicit noise.
The two differ by over an order of magnitude (<1% vs near 100%); one extra interaction step isn't why the volumes would be similar, so 'similar' contradicts the facts.
Clarity doesn't imply volume; explicit is extremely sparse precisely because it needs deliberate user action.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有信号可用的用户/样本比例;隐式信号覆盖几乎所有用户,显式只覆盖极少数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coverage is the fraction of users/items with any signal; implicit covers almost everyone, explicit covers very few.

scenario: 一次长停留可能是用户在认真看，也可能是他睡着了没关页面;一个 5 星评分则含义明确。
scenario_en: A long dwell could mean the user is engaged or fell asleep with the page open; a 5-star rating is unambiguous.
q: 隐式 vs 显式在「噪声 vs 清晰」这一维上如何取舍?
q_en: On the noise-vs-clarity axis, how do implicit and explicit signals trade off?
why: 隐式丰富但含糊:长停留=投入还是睡着?难分辨;显式稀疏但明确:5 星就是明确的正反馈。隐式需要去噪和校准,显式一条抵多条隐式的可信度。
why_en: Implicit is abundant but ambiguous (long dwell could be engagement or falling asleep) while explicit is sparse but clear (5 stars is unambiguous positive), so implicit needs denoising and explicit is more trustworthy per signal.
tradeoff: 隐式(丰富但含糊、需去噪) vs 显式(稀疏但明确、单条高可信)
options: 隐式信号和显式信号的噪声水平其实完全一样,只是两者的采集数量和覆盖用户的范围不同而已
隐式清晰、显式含糊,因为用户的行为不会撒谎而主动打的评分反而会撒谎
隐式丰富但含糊(长停留=投入?睡着?),显式稀疏但明确(5星=明确正反馈)
两者都不存在噪声,只要采集流程正确、埋点没出错，两种信号都是干净信号
options_en: Implicit and explicit signals actually have exactly the same noise level; only their collection volume and how much of the user base they cover differ.
Implicit is clear and explicit is ambiguous, because a user's behavior doesn't lie, while a deliberately given rating actually can.
Implicit is abundant but ambiguous (long dwell = engaged? asleep?), explicit is sparse but clear (5 stars = clear positive).
Neither has noise; as long as the collection pipeline is correct and the instrumentation has no bugs, both signal types are clean.
optionExplanations: 噪声水平不一样——隐式行为可有多种解读,显式评分含义单一,覆盖范围不同不代表信噪比相同。
说反了:隐式行为恰恰含糊(同一个停留多种解读),显式评分才是明确的。
对;隐式的模糊性正是需要显式来校准的原因,一次长停留说明不了投入度。
隐式行为天然含噪(误点、好奇、睡着),说「都无噪声」不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Noise levels differ — implicit behavior has multiple readings while an explicit rating has a single meaning; different coverage doesn't imply the same signal-to-noise ratio.
Backwards: implicit behavior is exactly the ambiguous one (a dwell has many readings), and explicit ratings are the clear ones.
Correct — implicit ambiguity is precisely why explicit is needed to calibrate; one long dwell can't prove engagement.
Implicit behavior is inherently noisy (mis-clicks, curiosity, falling asleep), so 'no noise' fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 行为与真实偏好之间的偏差;隐式信号噪声大(一个动作多种解读),显式噪声小。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Signal noise is the gap between behavior and true preference; implicit is noisy (one action, many readings), explicit is low-noise.

scenario: 要在产品里新增一路训练信号,得考虑采集这路信号要付出多少工程和用户成本。
scenario_en: Adding a new training signal to the product means weighing the engineering and user cost of collecting it.
q: 隐式 vs 显式在「采集成本」上如何取舍?
q_en: On collection cost, how do implicit and explicit signals trade off?
why: 隐式只要客户端埋点就能自动被动采集,单条几乎零成本;显式要额外的 UI 交互入口 + 用户愿意花时间填,每条数据更贵。所以隐式便宜量大、显式贵而稀。
why_en: Implicit needs only client-side instrumentation and collects passively at near-zero per-signal cost, while explicit needs UI affordances plus user willingness, making each data point more expensive.
tradeoff: 隐式(仅需埋点、被动、单条近零成本) vs 显式(需UI入口+用户意愿、单条更贵)
options: 隐式更贵,因为要处理海量行为日志的存储与计算;显式便宜,评分数据少、好存好查
两者采集成本完全一样,都只需要在客户端加一段自动上报的采集代码就行了
隐式只需客户端埋点、被动采集近零成本;显式需UI交互+用户意愿,每条更贵
采集成本只取决于最终的存储介质和容量,跟具体的采集方式完全无关
options_en: Implicit is costlier because you must store and process massive behavior logs; explicit is cheap since rating data is small and easy to store and query.
Both cost exactly the same to collect; each just needs a snippet of auto-reporting collection code added client-side.
Implicit needs only client instrumentation and collects passively at near-zero cost; explicit needs UI affordances + user willingness, costlier per signal.
Collection cost depends only on the final storage medium and capacity, completely unrelated to the specific collection method.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品本身就有强评分文化(如豆瓣、Yelp),显式采集的边际成本就低很多,可以更多依赖显式信号。
whenOtherWins_en: If the product has a strong rating culture (Douban, Yelp), the marginal cost of collecting explicit signals is much lower, so you can lean more on explicit.
optionExplanations: 把成本理解成存储量搞错了重点——真正贵的是显式要用户主动花时间,不是隐式的日志量。
成本不一样:隐式被动零打扰,显式要设计入口并说服用户,后者贵得多。
对;采集成本的关键是「要不要用户主动付出」,隐式不要、显式要,决定了每条数据的贵贱。
采集方式恰恰决定成本:被动埋点 vs 主动交互,存储只是小头。
optionExplanations_en: Framing cost as storage volume misses the point — the real cost is explicit demanding user effort, not implicit's log volume.
Costs differ: implicit is passive and unobtrusive, explicit needs an affordance and user persuasion, far costlier.
Correct — collection cost hinges on 'does the user have to act': implicit doesn't, explicit does, setting each point's price.
The collection method decides cost: passive instrumentation vs active interaction; storage is a minor part.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 App/网页里嵌入采集代码,自动记录用户行为事件,被动且不打扰用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Client-side instrumentation embeds collection code in the app/page to auto-log user behavior events, passively and unobtrusively.

termDefinitions.term: UI affordance / UI 交互入口
termDefinitions.meaning: 为让用户给显式反馈而设计的界面元素(评分星、点赞按钮),采集显式信号的前提。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UI affordance is an interface element (rating stars, like button) designed to let users give explicit feedback.

scenario: YouTube 既有海量的隐式观看时长,又有稀疏但清晰的显式点赞/点踩,要设计怎么一起用。
scenario_en: YouTube has abundant implicit watch-time and sparse-but-clear explicit thumbs up/down, and must design how to use them together.
q: MAANG 系统怎么融合隐式和显式信号?
q_en: How do MAANG systems fuse implicit and explicit signals?
why: 用隐式拿覆盖、用显式校准噪声:YouTube 主要靠隐式观看时长做覆盖广的训练信号,再用稀疏的显式点赞/点踩来校正、纠正隐式的噪声。两者分工——量靠隐式,准靠显式。
why_en: Use implicit for coverage and explicit to calibrate noise: YouTube weighs implicit watch-time for breadth and uses explicit thumbs to correct implicit noise.
tradeoff: 隐式做覆盖(量) + 显式做校准(准),分工而非二选一
options: 只用显式信号,因为它含义清晰,隐式信号噪声太大、不值得投入工程去处理
只用隐式信号,因为它量大覆盖全,显式信号太稀疏、边际价值太小不用管
把隐式和显式的原始分数简单相加合成一个分数,不区分权重和可信度
隐式做覆盖广的主信号,显式点赞/点踩用来校准、纠正隐式的噪声
options_en: Use only explicit signals, since they're unambiguous; implicit signals are too noisy to be worth the engineering effort to process.
Use only implicit signals, since they're plentiful and cover everyone; explicit signals are too sparse and low marginal value to bother with.
Simply add the raw implicit and explicit scores together into one score, with no distinction in weight or trustworthiness.
Implicit is the broad-coverage main signal, and explicit thumbs calibrate and correct implicit noise.
whenOtherWins: 如果某个任务的 ground truth 必须绝对可信(如安全/合规审核标签),就该以显式/人工标注为主,不能让隐式噪声混进关键标签。
whenOtherWins_en: If a task's ground truth must be absolutely trustworthy (safety/compliance labels), lean on explicit/human labels and keep implicit noise out of critical labels.
optionExplanations: 只用显式会因 <1% 的覆盖率严重欠数据,大多数用户没有任何显式信号可学。
只用隐式会把噪声全盘学进去,缺少显式锚点纠偏,长停留=睡着这类误读无法纠正。
不加权简单相加会让稀疏但可信的显式被海量隐式淹没,失去校准作用。
对;隐式给量、显式给准,用清晰的显式去校准嘈杂的隐式,是标准的融合分工。
optionExplanations_en: Explicit-only badly under-samples due to <1% coverage, leaving most users with no explicit signal to learn from.
Implicit-only absorbs all the noise with no explicit anchor to correct misreads like dwell = asleep.
Unweighted addition lets sparse-but-trustworthy explicit drown under massive implicit, losing its calibration role.
Correct — implicit gives volume, explicit gives accuracy, and using clear explicit to calibrate noisy implicit is the standard fusion split.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户观看某内容的时长,YouTube 主力隐式信号,覆盖广但含噪(睡着、后台播放)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Watch-time is how long a user watches content, YouTube's main implicit signal, broad but noisy (asleep, background play).

termDefinitions.meaning: 用可信的显式信号纠正隐式信号的系统性偏差,让训练标签更接近真实偏好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration uses trustworthy explicit signals to correct systematic bias in implicit signals so labels track true preference.

scenario: 给排序模型分配正/负标签时,不同行为对「用户真的想要」的意图强度不一样。
scenario_en: Assigning positive/negative labels for a ranking model, different behaviors carry different strength of 'the user truly wanted it'.
q: 信号丰富度层级(signal richness hierarchy)是什么,有什么用?
q_en: What is the signal richness hierarchy, and what's it for?
why: 按意图强度排:购买 > 点击 > 曝光。购买是最强的正意图信号,点击次之,单纯曝光最弱。这个层级直接指导排序里怎么分配正负标签——强意图当强正样本。
why_en: Ordered by intent strength: purchases > clicks > impressions, and it directly guides positive/negative label assignment in ranking, treating stronger intent as a stronger positive.
options: 曝光 > 点击 > 购买,越轻量、越不需要用户投入的行为越能反映真实意图
点击 > 购买 > 曝光,点击是最强的意图信号，因为点击次数远比购买次数多
购买 > 点击 > 曝光(按意图强度),用来指导排序里正负标签的分配
三者的意图强度完全相同,给排序模型分配标签时应该一视同仁地对待即可
options_en: Impressions > clicks > purchases; the lighter the action and the less effort it takes from the user, the truer it reflects real intent.
Clicks > purchases > impressions; clicks are the strongest intent signal because click counts far outnumber purchase counts.
Purchases > clicks > impressions (by intent strength), used to guide positive/negative label assignment in ranking.
All three carry exactly the same intent strength, so a ranking model's labels should just treat them all equally.
optionExplanations: 顺序反了:曝光只是被看到,意图最弱;购买付出了金钱,意图最强。
点击弱于购买——点了不一定买,购买才是真正掏钱的强意图确认。
对;购买>点击>曝光的意图梯度,决定哪种行为算强正样本、哪种只算弱信号。
三者意图强度差异明显,一视同仁会把强弱信号混为一谈,损害标签质量。
optionExplanations_en: Order reversed: an impression is merely being seen (weakest intent), while a purchase spends money (strongest).
Clicks are weaker than purchases — a click may not convert, while a purchase is the money-backed strong-intent confirmation.
Correct — the purchases > clicks > impressions intent gradient decides which action is a strong positive and which is only weak signal.
The three differ clearly in intent; treating them equally conflates strong and weak signals and hurts label quality.

termDefinitions.term: signal richness hierarchy / 信号丰富度层级
termDefinitions.meaning: 按意图强度给行为排序:购买 > 点击 > 曝光,指导正负标签分配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The signal richness hierarchy ranks behaviors by intent strength (purchases > clicks > impressions) to guide label assignment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容被展示给用户(不管有没有互动),意图信号最弱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is content shown to a user regardless of interaction, the weakest intent signal.

q: 把规范的事件采集管线(ingestion pipeline)排成正确的数据流顺序:
q_en: Order the canonical event-ingestion pipeline data flow correctly:
steps: 分布式消息broker(Kafka/Kinesis)接收结构化事件
客户端埋点发出结构化事件
流处理器(Flink/Spark Streaming)用画像/会话上下文富化
两个sink:feature store(在线服务) + data lake(离线训练)
why: 数据流:埋点发事件→broker(Kafka/Kinesis)缓冲→流处理器富化画像/会话→双sink落地(feature store在线、data lake离线)。broker解耦生产消费,双sink分服务在线离线。
why_en: Client instrumentation emits events, a Kafka/Kinesis broker buffers them, Flink/Spark stream processors enrich with profile/session context, then two sinks land it: a feature store for online serving and a data lake for offline training.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["客户端埋点"] --> B["消息broker
Kafka/Kinesis"] B --> S["流处理器
Flink/Spark"] S --> F["feature store
在线服务"] S --> D["data lake
离线训练"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收并缓冲事件流、解耦生产者与消费者的分布式系统(Kafka、Kinesis)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message broker is a distributed system that receives and buffers event streams, decoupling producers from consumers (Kafka, Kinesis).

termDefinitions.meaning: 实时消费事件流并做富化/聚合的引擎(Flink、Spark Streaming)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stream processor is an engine that consumes event streams in real time and enriches/aggregates them (Flink, Spark Streaming).

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中存储并按需低延迟提供模型特征的系统,服务在线推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally stores and serves model features at low latency for online inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存原始/半结构化数据的大规模离线存储(S3/HDFS),供离线训练与分析。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data lake is large-scale offline storage for raw/semi-structured data (S3/HDFS) used for offline training and analytics.

scenario: 事件量达到每秒数百万条,既要横向扩展,又要保住同一用户事件的先后顺序。
scenario_en: Events hit millions per second; you need horizontal scale while preserving the order of one user's events.
q: Kafka 用「按 key 分区」解决了什么?
q_en: What does Kafka's 'partitioning by key' solve?
why: 按 key(如用户/会话 ID)分区,让事件横向摊到多分区扩到每秒百万级,同时保住每个分区内的有序性——同一用户的事件进同一分区、保持先后。既扩规模又不打乱单用户时序。
why_en: Partitioning by key (user/session ID) spreads events across partitions to scale to millions/sec while preserving per-partition ordering, so one user's events stay ordered in one partition.
tradeoff: 按key分区(横向扩展+分区内有序) vs 单分区(全局有序但扛不住吞吐)
options: 解决了数据加密,分区用的 key 本身就被当成加密密钥来使用
解决了去重,同一个 key 的事件进入同一分区后会被自动合并成一条,减轻下游负担
按 key(用户/会话ID)分区:横向扩到百万/秒 + 保住每个分区内事件有序
解决了压缩,分区数量越多单条事件的数据体积就会被压得越小
options_en: It solves encryption; the key used for partitioning is itself treated as the encryption key.
It solves deduplication; once same-key events land in the same partition they get auto-merged into one, easing load downstream.
Partition by key (user/session ID): scale horizontally to millions/sec + preserve per-partition event ordering.
It solves compression; the more partitions there are, the smaller each event's data size gets compressed to.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务需要跨用户的全局严格有序(罕见),按 key 分区就不够,得用单分区或额外排序机制,代价是吞吐大降。
whenOtherWins_en: If the business needs strict global ordering across users (rare), key partitioning isn't enough — use a single partition or extra ordering, at a large throughput cost.
optionExplanations: 分区 key 是路由用的哈希键,不是加密密钥,与加密无关。
分区不做去重,同 key 事件只是进同一分区,不会自动合并,下游负担也不会因此减轻。
对;按 key 分区同时拿到横向扩展和分区内有序,正是高吞吐+保序的经典解法。
分区是为并行和有序,不是压缩,分区数与数据体积无关。
optionExplanations_en: The partition key is a routing hash key, not an encryption key, unrelated to encryption.
Partitioning doesn't dedup; same-key events just land in the same partition and don't auto-merge, so downstream load isn't eased by this either.
Correct — partitioning by key gets both horizontal scale and in-partition ordering, the classic high-throughput-plus-order solution.
Partitioning is for parallelism and ordering, not compression; partition count is unrelated to data size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 key 把事件流拆到多个并行分区,实现横向扩展并保住每个分区内的有序性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioning splits an event stream by key across parallel partitions for horizontal scale while keeping order within each partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一分区里的事件严格按写入先后被消费,同 key 事件因此保序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-partition ordering means events in one partition are consumed strictly in write order, so same-key events stay ordered.

scenario: 同一份用户事件流,既要喂在线特征服务、又要喂离线训练、还要喂实时监控,三个下游互不影响。
scenario_en: One user event stream must feed online feature serving, offline training, and real-time monitoring, with the three downstreams not interfering.
q: Kafka 的「消费组独立性」带来什么好处?
q_en: What does Kafka's 'consumer group independence' provide?
why: 多个下游各建自己的消费组,独立地读同一条流、各自维护自己的读进度(offset),互不干扰。一份数据可被在线服务、离线训练、监控同时消费,不用复制多份流。
why_en: Multiple downstreams form separate consumer groups, each reading the same stream and tracking its own offset independently, so one stream feeds serving, training, and monitoring without interfering.
options: 多个下游各建消费组、独立读同一条流并各自维护offset,互不干扰
所有下游共用同一个读进度,读得慢的消费者会拖住读得快的那个
一条流在同一时刻只能被一个下游消费,其它下游要单独复制一份新流
消费组读取事件后会自动把它从 topic 里删除,后来的下游读不到历史
options_en: Multiple downstreams form separate consumer groups, each reading the same stream and tracking its own offset independently, without interference.
All downstreams share the exact same read offset, so a slow consumer holds back a fast one.
A stream can be consumed by only one downstream at a time; other downstreams must each copy their own new stream.
A consumer group auto-deletes an event from the topic once it's read, so later downstreams can't read the history.
optionExplanations: 对;每个消费组独立 offset,一份流被多个下游并行消费而互不影响,是复用数据的关键。
消费组独立性恰恰避免了共享进度,慢消费者不会拖住快消费者。
一条流可被任意多个消费组读,不需要为每个下游复制流。
Kafka 按保留期存事件,读了不立即删,后来的消费组仍可读历史。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — each group tracks its own offset, letting one stream be consumed in parallel by many downstreams without interference, the key to reusing data.
Consumer group independence precisely avoids shared offsets, so a slow consumer won't hold back a fast one.
One stream can be read by arbitrarily many consumer groups; no per-downstream copy is needed.
Kafka retains events by a retention period and doesn't delete on read, so later groups can still read history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组共同消费一个topic的消费者,各消费组独立维护自己的读进度(offset)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumers jointly reading a topic; each group tracks its own read offset independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费组在分区里已读到的位置,决定下一条从哪读,各组互不影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a consumer group's read position in a partition, deciding where to read next, independent per group.

scenario: 如果同一个点击事件被重复写进流两次,训练时这条正样本就被算了两遍。
scenario_en: If the same click event is written to the stream twice, that positive sample gets counted twice at training time.
q: Kafka 的 exactly-once 语义为 ML 数据解决了什么问题?
q_en: What does Kafka's exactly-once semantics solve for ML data?
why: 靠幂等生产者 + 事务性消费者保证每个事件不重不漏地处理一次,防止重复事件制造重复/有偏标签。重复的正样本会悄悄放大某类信号、扭曲目标函数,exactly-once 从源头堵住这种偏差。
why_en: Idempotent producers plus transactional consumers ensure each event is processed exactly once, preventing duplicate events from creating duplicate or biased labels that would silently skew the objective.
options: 保证事件在传输链路上被加密,防止中间人窃听到点击事件的内容
保证事件被永久保存在 broker 上,不管保留期设置多长都不会被清理删除
靠幂等生产者+事务性消费者保证每事件处理一次,防重复事件制造重复/有偏标签
保证同一批事件在存储时按字母顺序重新排列,方便后续按名称查询
options_en: It guarantees events are encrypted in transit, preventing a man-in-the-middle from eavesdropping on click-event content.
It guarantees events are stored forever on the broker, and no matter how the retention period is set, they won't get cleaned up.
Idempotent producers + transactional consumers ensure each event is processed once, preventing duplicate events from creating duplicate/biased labels.
It guarantees a batch of events is re-sorted alphabetically in storage, making later name-based queries easier.
optionExplanations: 它管的是加密传输，不是「处理几次」——跟 exactly-once 要解决的问题不是一回事。
保留期是存储策略，不是 exactly-once 要保证的处理语义，两者管的是不同的事。
对;幂等+事务确保不重不漏一次,直接防住重复事件把某类标签悄悄放大成偏差。
字母排序是查询便利问题，exactly-once 只解决重复处理，不涉及排序。
optionExplanations_en: It concerns encrypted transport, not 'how many times processed' — a different problem from what exactly-once solves.
Retention is a storage policy, not the processing semantics exactly-once guarantees; the two govern different things.
Correct — idempotent plus transactional ensures once-and-only-once, directly preventing duplicate events from silently inflating a label class into bias.
Alphabetical order is a query convenience, not something exactly-once touches — it only solves duplicate processing.

termDefinitions.term: exactly-once semantics / 恰好一次语义
termDefinitions.meaning: 每个事件被不重不漏地处理恰好一次,靠幂等生产者+事务性消费者实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once semantics processes each event once and only once, via idempotent producers and transactional consumers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 即使重发同一消息,broker 也只记录一次,避免生产端重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent producer ensures the broker records a resent message only once, avoiding producer-side duplicates.

scenario: 团队全栈在 AWS 上,要选事件流平台:自建 Kafka 还是用托管的 Kinesis。
scenario_en: An all-AWS team must pick an event-streaming platform: self-run Kafka or managed Kinesis.
q: Kafka vs Kinesis,取舍在哪一维?
q_en: Kafka vs Kinesis — on which dimension do they trade off?
why: 取舍在「灵活性 vs 托管便利」:Kafka灵活、生态强但要自运维;Kinesis是AWS托管(直连Lambda/Firehose)省运维但灵活性略低。全栈AWS、想少运维选Kinesis。
why_en: The axis is flexibility vs managed convenience: Kafka offers richer partitioning/consumer flexibility but you self-operate it, while Kinesis is AWS-native managed (integrates with Lambda/Firehose/Redshift) with less flexibility.
tradeoff: Kafka(灵活、生态强、自运维) vs Kinesis(AWS托管、省运维、灵活性略低)
options: 取舍在灵活性 vs 托管便利:Kafka灵活但自运维;Kinesis AWS托管省运维但灵活性略低
取舍在传输准确率:Kafka 的消息传输天然更准,Kinesis 在高吞吐下会丢数据
取舍在可用编程语言:Kafka 生产者消费者只能用 Java 写,Kinesis 只能用 Python 写
两者在架构和特性上完全等价,选哪个纯粹只看团队个人喜好即可
options_en: The axis is flexibility vs managed convenience: Kafka is flexible but self-operated; Kinesis is AWS-managed with less flexibility.
The axis is transmission accuracy: Kafka's message delivery is inherently more accurate, while Kinesis loses data under high throughput.
The axis is available languages: Kafka producers/consumers can only be written in Java, Kinesis only in Python.
The two are fully equivalent in architecture and features; the choice is purely down to the team's personal taste.
whenOtherWins: 如果团队要跨云或需要极致的分区/消费灵活性,Kafka 更合适;只有全栈锁定 AWS、且想最小化运维时,Kinesis 才反超。
whenOtherWins_en: If the team is multi-cloud or needs maximal partitioning/consumer flexibility, Kafka fits better; Kinesis only wins when fully AWS-locked and minimizing ops.
optionExplanations: 对;真正的区分维是灵活性 vs 托管便利,不是谁更准,两者都可靠。
Kinesis 不会天然丢数据,两者都提供可靠投递,准确率不是区分维。
两者都支持多语言 SDK,「Java-only/Python-only」是编造的限制。
两者在运维、灵活性、生态上系统性不同,不是凭喜好随便选。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the real axis is flexibility vs managed convenience, not accuracy; both are reliable.
Kinesis doesn't inherently lose data; both offer reliable delivery, so accuracy isn't the axis.
Both support multi-language SDKs; 'Java-only/Python-only' is a fabricated limit.
They differ systematically in ops, flexibility, and ecosystem, not a matter of preference.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 原生的托管事件流服务,用 shard 分片,直连 Lambda/Firehose/Redshift,省运维但灵活性略低于 Kafka。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis is AWS's managed event-streaming service using shards, integrating with Lambda/Firehose/Redshift, low-ops but less flexible than Kafka.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商代运维的服务,换钱省掉自建集群与维护人力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A managed service is cloud-operated infrastructure, trading money for saved cluster build-and-maintain effort.

scenario: 一个 Kafka 数据管线没有 schema registry。某天上游悄悄把一个字段从整数改成字符串,没人发现,模型继续训练。
scenario_en: A Kafka pipeline has no schema registry. One day upstream silently changes a field from int to string; nobody notices and the model keeps training.
q: 缺少 schema registry 的管线,最危险的失败模式是什么?
q_en: For a pipeline lacking a schema registry, what's the most dangerous failure mode?
why: 静默数据腐坏:没有 schema 契约(Avro/Protobuf)约束,上游字段类型一变没人察觉,模型在被污染的标签上继续训练,却不报任何错、不触发告警。比 broker 宕机更危险——宕机会报警,腐坏无声无息。
why_en: Silent data corruption: without a schema contract (Avro/Protobuf), an upstream type change goes unnoticed, the model trains on corrupted labels, and no error or alert fires — worse than broker downtime, which at least alarms.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["上游改字段类型"] --> N["无schema校验"] N --> C["标签被污染"] C --> M["模型静默退化
不报错不告警"]
options: broker 宕机导致整条管线彻底停摆,但监控会立刻报警、工程师能马上介入
静默数据腐坏:字段类型悄变没人察觉,模型在被污染的标签上训练,不报错不告警
磁盘写满导致新事件写不进去,存储监控会立刻发现并触发告警通知值班
网络抖动导致部分事件延迟到达,重试和补偿机制会自动把它们处理掉
options_en: Broker downtime brings the whole pipeline to a total halt, but monitoring alarms immediately and engineers can jump in right away.
Silent data corruption: a field type changes unnoticed, the model trains on corrupted labels, with no error or alert.
A full disk blocks new events from being written, and storage monitoring catches it immediately and pages whoever's on call.
Network jitter delays some events, and retry/compensation mechanisms automatically handle them.
optionExplanations: broker 宕机确实糟但会报警,可被立即发现修复,不是「最危险」的那种无声失败。
对;无 schema 校验的字段漂移无声无息地污染标签,模型悄悄退化才是最危险的,因为没人知道。
磁盘写满是显性故障、有监控兜底,不属于「静默」这一类隐蔽失败。
网络延迟是常见可观测问题,有重试/补偿,不是缺 schema registry 的核心风险。
optionExplanations_en: Broker downtime is bad but alarms and gets fixed fast, not the 'most dangerous' silent kind of failure.
Correct — without schema validation, field drift silently corrupts labels and the model degrades unnoticed, most dangerous precisely because nobody knows.
A full disk is an explicit fault with monitoring backstop, not the 'silent' category of failure.
Network delay is a common observable issue with retries/compensation, not the core risk of a missing schema registry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中存储并强制事件schema契约(Avro/Protobuf)的服务,阻止不兼容的字段变更悄悄进入管线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema registry centrally stores and enforces event schema contracts (Avro/Protobuf), blocking incompatible field changes from silently entering the pipeline.

termDefinitions.term: silent data corruption / 静默数据腐坏
termDefinitions.meaning: 数据被破坏但系统不报错、不告警,模型在脏数据上退化而无人察觉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Silent data corruption is data getting broken with no error or alert, so the model degrades on dirty data unnoticed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两种带schema的序列化格式,用schema契约描述字段类型,支持schema演进校验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Avro and Protobuf are schema-based serialization formats that describe field types via a contract and support schema-evolution checks.

scenario: 线上 schema 需要改动(加字段、改类型),但老的生产者和消费者不能全部同时升级。
scenario_en: A live schema must change (add a field, change a type), but old producers and consumers can't all upgrade at once.
q: schema 演进的向后/向前兼容分别指什么?
q_en: What do backward and forward schema-evolution compatibility mean?
why: 向后兼容=新消费者能读老数据(老生产者不升级也行);向前兼容=老消费者能读新数据(新生产者先升级也不崩)。有了兼容规则,生产者和消费者可以分批滚动升级,不必同时切换。
why_en: Backward compatibility lets new consumers read old data, and forward compatibility lets old consumers read new data, so producers and consumers can upgrade in rolling batches rather than all at once.
options: 向后兼容=消费者只能读旧版本数据、向前兼容=消费者只能读新版本数据,两者互斥不能共存
向后兼容=序列化后数据变小、向前兼容=序列化后数据变大,跟版本兼容性无关
两者是同一件事的两种说法,都是指数据经过压缩后能被正常读取
向后兼容=新消费者能读老数据;向前兼容=老消费者能读新数据,支持分批滚动升级
options_en: Backward compatibility = consumers can only read old-version data, forward compatibility = consumers can only read new-version data; the two are mutually exclusive.
Backward compatibility = serialized data gets smaller, forward compatibility = serialized data gets bigger, unrelated to version compatibility.
They're two names for the same thing, both meaning data can be read normally after being compressed.
Backward compatibility = new consumers read old data; forward compatibility = old consumers read new data, enabling rolling upgrades.
optionExplanations: 两者不互斥,良好设计的 schema 常同时满足向后和向前兼容。
兼容性讲的是不同版本能否互读,不是数据大小。
兼容性与压缩无关,不是同义词。
对;向后让新读老、向前让老读新,正是分批升级不停机的关键。
optionExplanations_en: They aren't exclusive; a well-designed schema often satisfies both backward and forward compatibility.
Compatibility is about whether versions can inter-read, not data size.
Compatibility is unrelated to compression and they aren't synonyms.
Correct — backward lets new read old, forward lets old read new, the key to zero-downtime rolling upgrades.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新版消费者能正确读取用老 schema 产生的旧数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backward compatibility means new consumers can correctly read old data produced under an older schema.

termDefinitions.meaning: 老版消费者能正确读取用新 schema 产生的新数据(忽略新增字段)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Forward compatibility means old consumers can correctly read new data produced under a newer schema (ignoring added fields).

scenario: Flink 消费者处理速度跟不上 Kafka 的写入速度,消息在上游越积越多。
scenario_en: A Flink consumer can't keep up with Kafka's write rate, and messages pile up upstream.
q: 消费者跟不上生产速度(backpressure)时,有哪些应对手段?
q_en: When a consumer lags the producer (backpressure), what are the options?
why: 三条路:缓冲(在内存里暂存,但有内存压力)、限流(rate-limit 降低摄入速度)、或丢弃低优先级事件(shed)。核心是别让积压压垮消费者,必要时主动取舍——先保住高优先级数据。
why_en: Three options: buffer in memory (at the cost of memory pressure), rate-limit ingestion, or shed low-priority events, the point being not to let the backlog crush the consumer.
tradeoff: 缓冲(不丢数据、吃内存) vs 限流(稳但整体变慢) vs 丢弃低优先级(保关键、丢部分)
options: 唯一办法是无限扩内存把所有积压都缓存下来,绝不丢任何一条事件
直接把 Kafka 集群和上游生产者全部停掉,等 Flink 消费追上积压进度后再重新启动
缓冲(吃内存)、限流(降摄入)、或丢弃低优先级事件(shed),别让积压压垮消费者
让上游生产者主动放慢速度、跟消费者保持一致,这样就永远不会产生积压
options_en: The only option is to expand memory without limit to buffer the whole backlog, never dropping a single event.
Just shut the whole Kafka cluster and the upstream producers down, then restart once Flink's consumption has caught up on the backlog.
Buffer (memory cost), rate-limit (slow ingestion), or shed low-priority events, so the backlog doesn't crush the consumer.
Have the upstream producer deliberately slow down to match the consumer, so a backlog never forms.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有事件都同等关键、绝对不能丢(如金融交易日志),就不能 shed,得靠扩容消费者+缓冲扛住,代价是成本上升。
whenOtherWins_en: If every event is equally critical and can't be dropped (financial transaction logs), you can't shed — scale out consumers and buffer instead, at higher cost.
optionExplanations: 无限扩内存不现实,内存有上限,持续积压最终会 OOM,缓冲只是三选项之一不是唯一。
停 Kafka 和生产者会丢实时性、造成更大积压,是回避不是应对 backpressure。
对;缓冲/限流/丢弃是标准三招,按数据重要性取舍,先保关键流。
强行拖慢生产者等于牺牲上游吞吐,通常不可行,且不是处理瞬时积压的正解。
optionExplanations_en: Infinite memory is unreal; memory is bounded and sustained backlog eventually OOMs, so buffering is one of three options, not the only one.
Stopping Kafka and the producers loses real-timeness and grows the backlog even more, dodging rather than handling backpressure.
Correct — buffer/rate-limit/shed are the standard three, chosen by data importance, protecting the critical stream first.
Force-slowing the producer sacrifices upstream throughput, usually infeasible and not the right fix for a transient backlog.

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游消费速度跟不上上游生产速度导致积压,需靠缓冲/限流/丢弃来化解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure is when downstream consumption lags upstream production, causing backlog, handled by buffering, rate-limiting, or shedding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动丢掉低优先级事件以保住关键数据流不被积压压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shedding deliberately drops low-priority events to keep the critical stream from being crushed by backlog.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源分布式消息broker，生产者写入、消费者读取，用于高吞吐事件流传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is an open-source distributed message broker where producers write and consumers read, used for high-throughput event streaming.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源流处理引擎，实时消费事件流并做富化、聚合、状态计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is an open-source stream-processing engine that consumes event streams in real time to enrich, aggregate, and compute state.

scenario: 富化后的事件要落地到两个去处:一个供在线模型实时取特征,一个供离线批量训练。
scenario_en: Enriched events land in two destinations: one for online models to fetch features in real time, one for offline batch training.
q: feature store 和 data lake 两个 sink 分工是什么?
q_en: What's the division between the feature store and data lake sinks?
why: feature store 服务在线推理:低延迟、按 key 取最新特征,给实时预测用;data lake(S3/HDFS)存海量原始/历史数据供离线训练与分析。一个求快、一个求全,双写让在线和离线各取所需。
why_en: The feature store serves online inference with low-latency latest-feature lookups, while the data lake (S3/HDFS) stores massive raw/historical data for offline training and analytics.
tradeoff: feature store(低延迟、在线取特征) vs data lake(大容量、离线训练/分析)
options: feature store 服务在线推理;data lake 存历史数据供离线训练
两个 sink 存完全一样的数据,只是互为备份
feature store 存放离线训练数据,data lake 专门负责在线服务
两者都只供离线用,在线服务不从任何 sink 取数
options_en: The feature store serves online inference; the data lake stores historical data for offline training.
The two sinks store identical data, just as backups of each other.
The feature store holds offline training data, and the data lake is specifically responsible for online serving.
Both are offline-only; online serving reads from no sink.
optionExplanations: 对,feature store给在线推理供最新特征、低延迟读;data lake给离线训练存原始历史,双写分工不冲突。
两者存的数据形态和用途不同,不是简单互备:一个存最新特征、一个存全量历史。
角色说反了:feature store才是承担在线服务的一侧,data lake才是负责离线存储的一侧,两者分工不能对调。
在线服务正是从feature store里实时取特征,「不从任何 sink 取数」的说法站不住。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one side answers reads fast with the newest features, the other keeps the full raw history so batch training can run; each sink owns its lane.
The two store different shapes and serve different purposes, not simple mirrors: one holds latest features, one holds full history.
Roles reversed: it's the feature store that serves online reads, and the data lake that's the offline store — the two can't be swapped.
Online serving reads its latest features straight out of that same online store, so 'reads from no sink' doesn't hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两种大规模对象/分布式文件存储,常作为 data lake 的底座存海量离线数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 and HDFS are large-scale object/distributed file stores commonly backing a data lake for massive offline data.

scenario: 自有行为数据不够,考虑从第三方数据商(如 Acxiom、Oracle Data Cloud)购买人口/地理/意图数据来富化特征。
scenario_en: Own behavioral data is thin, so you consider buying demographic/location/intent data from third-party brokers (Acxiom, Oracle Data Cloud) to enrich features.
q: 用第三方合作数据,合同里必须约定什么?
q_en: When using third-party partnership data, what must the contract specify?
why: 合同必须明确允许的使用范围、数据保留期限、以及审计权。第三方数据不是买来随便用——用途越界、留存超期都可能违约违规,审计权保证可追溯合规。
why_en: The contract must specify permitted use, retention period, and audit rights, because third-party data can't be used freely — overstepping use or retention risks breach and non-compliance.
tradeoff: 买第三方数据(快速富化特征) vs 自建采集(慢但可控、无合规/来源风险)
options: 只要跟数据商谈好价格就行,买回来的数据想怎么用、留多久都行
合同必须约定允许的使用范围、数据保留期限、审计权,越界即违约违规
只需要在合同里约定数据格式,后续的合规审查完全是数据商单方面的责任
买来的数据因为不是自己采集的,所以不受 GDPR/CCPA 等任何法规约束
options_en: Just agree on price with the broker; once bought, you can use the data however you like and keep it as long as you want.
The contract must specify permitted use, retention period, and audit rights; overstepping is breach and non-compliance.
The contract only needs to specify data format; ongoing compliance review is solely the broker's responsibility.
Because you didn't collect the purchased data yourself, it's exempt from GDPR/CCPA or any other regulation.
optionExplanations: 「买来随便用」会踩用途/留存红线,第三方数据的使用范围恰恰是合同核心。
对;使用范围+保留期+审计权是第三方数据合同必备,越界直接触发违约与合规风险。
格式只是技术细节,合规是买方也要承担的责任,不能全推给数据商。
外购数据同样受 GDPR/CCPA 等约束,「不是自己收集就免责」是错误认知。
optionExplanations_en: 'Use it however' crosses use/retention lines; the permitted scope of third-party data is exactly the contract's core.
Correct — permitted use + retention + audit rights are contract essentials, and overstepping triggers breach and compliance risk.
Format is a technical detail; compliance is also the buyer's responsibility and can't be fully offloaded to the broker.
Purchased data is still bound by GDPR/CCPA; 'not self-collected so exempt' is a false belief.

termDefinitions.term: third-party data broker / 第三方数据商
termDefinitions.meaning: 出售人口/地理/意图等数据的公司(Acxiom、Oracle Data Cloud),使用受合同与法规约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A third-party data broker (Acxiom, Oracle Data Cloud) sells demographic/location/intent data whose use is bound by contract and regulation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 合同赋予的核查数据来源与使用是否合规的权利,保证可追溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Audit rights are the contractual right to verify data provenance and compliant use, ensuring traceability.

whenOtherWins: 如果已有充足的第一方行为数据,或第三方数据的合规/来源风险不可接受,就该自建采集而非外购。
whenOtherWins_en: If you already have ample first-party behavioral data, or the third-party compliance/provenance risk is unacceptable, build your own collection instead of buying.

scenario: 想爬取公开网页来 bootstrap 物品特征或做 NLP 预训练语料。
scenario_en: You want to crawl public web pages to bootstrap item features or gather NLP pre-training corpus.
q: 用爬虫采集数据时,工程上要遵守哪些规矩?
q_en: When scraping for data, what engineering norms must you follow?
why: 遵守 robots.txt(尊重站点的抓取声明)、限速(rate-limit,别压垮对方服务器)、去重(dedup,避免重复内容污染数据)。爬取能快速 bootstrap 特征/预训练语料,但要做负责任的爬虫。
why_en: Respect robots.txt, rate-limit to avoid overloading the target, and dedup to avoid polluting data with repeats, so scraping bootstraps features/corpus responsibly.
tradeoff: 爬取(快速bootstrap特征/语料) vs 合规风险(需守robots.txt、限速、法律未定)
options: 尽可能快地全量抓取全站页面,不用管站点的 robots.txt 声明,数据越多越好
抓完的页面内容直接拿去用,不用做去重、也不用限制抓取的频率
只抓需要登录才能看到的私有页面,公开页面对模型训练没有价值
遵守 robots.txt + 限速(别压垮对方) + 去重(避免重复内容污染数据)
options_en: Crawl the entire site as fast as possible, ignoring its robots.txt declarations — more data is always better.
Use the scraped page content directly, with no dedup and no limit on crawl frequency.
Only scrape login-gated private pages; public pages have no value for model training.
Respect robots.txt + rate-limit (don't overload the target) + dedup (avoid repeat content polluting data).
optionExplanations: 无视 robots.txt 且全速抓取会压垮站点、招致封禁甚至法律风险,不是负责任的做法。
不去重会让重复内容污染训练数据,不控频率会压垮对方,两者都不能省。
公开页面正是爬取的主要目标,抓私有登录页反而涉及更严重的越权风险。
对;robots.txt+限速+去重是负责任爬虫三要素,既拿到数据又控住合规和质量风险。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring robots.txt and crawling full-speed overloads the site and risks bans or legal exposure — not responsible.
No dedup lets repeats pollute training data, and no rate control overloads the target; neither can be skipped.
Public pages are the main scraping target; scraping login-gated pages raises far more serious access-violation risk.
Correct — robots.txt + rate-limit + dedup are the three responsible-scraping essentials, getting data while controlling compliance and quality risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网站根目录声明允许/禁止爬取哪些路径的文件,负责任的爬虫应遵守。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: robots.txt is a site's root-level file declaring which paths crawlers may or may not fetch; responsible crawlers respect it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 删除重复内容,避免同一文本多次进入训练数据造成偏差与浪费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dedup removes duplicate content so the same text doesn't enter training data repeatedly, avoiding bias and waste.

whenOtherWins: 如果目标站点提供官方 API 或授权数据集,就走 API/授权渠道而非爬取,更稳定合规、无封禁风险。
whenOtherWins_en: If the target offers an official API or licensed dataset, use that instead of scraping for stability, compliance, and no ban risk.

scenario: 想用免费的公开数据集给模型做富化或预训练,降低自采成本。
scenario_en: You want free public datasets to enrich or pre-train the model, cutting self-collection cost.
q: 公开/开放数据集在 ML 里扮演什么角色?举一个 LLM 相关例子。
q_en: What role do public/open datasets play in ML? Give one LLM-related example.
why: 免费的富化/预训练来源:Wikidata、Common Crawl、政府/学术语料。Common Crawl(大规模网页抓取快照)是很多 LLM 网页文本训练数据的底座——公开数据集能大幅降低自采成本、扩大覆盖。
why_en: They are free enrichment/pre-training sources (Wikidata, Common Crawl, gov/academic corpora); Common Crawl underpins much of the web-text training data for LLMs.
options: 免费的富化/预训练来源，如 Wikidata、Common Crawl；Common Crawl 撑起不少 LLM 网页语料
公开数据集虽然免费,但普遍存在标注不一致、噪声很大、版权来源也说不清楚等问题,还可能引发法律纠纷,不适合直接部署到生产环境
公开数据集在多数许可证下只允许用于课堂教学和学术演示,一旦被商业公司拿去训练模型对外提供服务就一律构成违法
只要是标注为「公开」的数据集,使用前都必须先联系发布方签署书面付费授权协议,不存在能直接免费使用的情况
options_en: Free enrichment/pre-training sources like Wikidata and Common Crawl; Common Crawl underpins much of the LLM web corpus.

Public datasets are free, but commonly suffer from inconsistent labeling, heavy noise, and unclear copyright provenance, which can even trigger legal disputes, unsuited for shipping directly in production.
Under most licenses, public datasets are permitted only for classroom teaching and academic demos; any commercial company training a model to offer a service is automatically illegal.
Any dataset labeled 'public' still requires contacting the publisher beforehand to sign a paid written license — there's no such thing as using it directly for free.
optionExplanations: 对;Wikidata/Common Crawl 等是免费富化与预训练底座,Common Crawl 尤其是 LLM 网页语料主力。
生产环境的大模型普遍靠 Common Crawl 等公开语料预训练,「质量太差、会惹官司不能用」的说法与这一事实相悖。
多数开放数据集允许商用(视许可证),「商用一律违法」过度绝对。
「开放/公开」的核心正是免费可取,说必须付费与定义矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — Wikidata/Common Crawl are free enrichment and pre-training bases, with Common Crawl a mainstay of LLM web corpus.
Production-scale LLMs are widely pre-trained on public corpora like Common Crawl, so 'too low-quality and legally risky to use' contradicts that fact.
Most open datasets permit commercial use (per license); 'commercial use always illegal' is overly absolute.
'Open/public' means freely available at its core, so 'must be paid' contradicts the definition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大规模、定期更新的公开网页抓取快照,是许多 LLM 网页文本训练数据的来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common Crawl is a large, regularly updated public snapshot of crawled web pages, a source of much LLM web-text training data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维基媒体的结构化开放知识库,常用于实体/知识富化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wikidata is Wikimedia's structured open knowledge base, often used for entity/knowledge enrichment.

scenario: 团队想「先把所有能采的用户行为都存下来,以后说不定有用」。
scenario_en: The team wants to 'log every user behavior we can, just in case it's useful later'.
q: GDPR/CCPA 的「数据最小化」原则,如何约束这种做法?
q_en: How does GDPR/CCPA data minimization constrain 'log everything just in case'?
why: 要用户同意 + 数据最小化:只能为明确目的收集必要数据,不能「先囤着以后再说」。这是设计约束不是可选项——违反最小化原则本身就违规,不管数据将来有没有用。
why_en: Consent plus data minimization means collecting only necessary data for a stated purpose, so 'hoard just in case' is itself a violation regardless of future usefulness.
options: 完全没有约束,只要把用户身份信息做了匿名化处理,想存多少行为数据都行
要用户同意+数据最小化:只为明确目的收必要数据,不能「先囤着以后再说」,违反即违规
只要把这些行为数据存在公司自己的服务器上,就完全不受 GDPR/CCPA 等法规管辖
数据最小化原则只是一条行业建议,不遵守也不影响产品能不能正常上线
options_en: No constraint at all — as long as user identity is anonymized, you can store as much behavioral data as you want.
Consent + data minimization: collect only necessary data for a stated purpose; 'hoard just in case' is itself a violation.
As long as this behavioral data is stored on the company's own servers, it's completely outside GDPR/CCPA and similar regulations' jurisdiction.
Data minimization is just an industry recommendation; ignoring it doesn't affect whether the product can ship.
optionExplanations: 匿名化不豁免最小化原则,且行为数据常可再识别,「随便存」仍然违规。
对;GDPR/CCPA 把最小化设为硬约束,无明确目的的囤积本身就违规,不看将来是否有用。
GDPR/CCPA 按数据主体所在地适用,存自己服务器不豁免这些监管。
最小化是法定原则不是建议,违反会带来合规风险,直接影响可部署性。
optionExplanations_en: Anonymization doesn't exempt minimization, and behavioral data is often re-identifiable, so 'store freely' still violates.
Correct — GDPR/CCPA make minimization a hard constraint; hoarding with no stated purpose violates regardless of future usefulness.
GDPR/CCPA apply based on the data subject's location; storing on your own servers grants no exemption from either.
Minimization is a legal principle, not advice; violating it creates compliance risk that affects deployability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只为明确、必要的目的收集所需的最少数据,禁止「先囤着以后再说」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data minimization collects only the minimum data needed for a stated, necessary purpose, forbidding 'hoard just in case'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加州消费者隐私法,与 GDPR 类似,赋予用户知情/删除/退出等数据权利。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act) is a California privacy law like GDPR, granting users rights to know, delete, and opt out.

scenario: 有人主张「公开网页数据爬取绝对合法」,你要在面试里给一个更准确的说法。
scenario_en: Someone claims 'scraping public web data is definitely legal'; you need a more accurate stance in an interview.
q: 爬取公开数据的法律状态,准确的表述是什么?(hiQ v. LinkedIn)
q_en: What's the accurate statement on the legality of scraping public data? (hiQ v. LinkedIn)
why: 尚不确定、还在演变:hiQ v. LinkedIn 一案表明,爬取公开数据不必然构成 CFAA(计算机欺诈和滥用法)违规,但法律仍在变化。面试里该说「法律未定、需谨慎评估」,而不是「绝对合法/绝对违法」。
why_en: It's unsettled and evolving: hiQ v. LinkedIn suggested scraping public data isn't necessarily a CFAA violation, but the law keeps changing, so say 'unsettled, assess carefully' rather than an absolute.
options: 绝对合法:只要网页是公开可访问的,谁都能随意爬取,不受任何服务条款或法律约束
绝对违法:只要用程序自动访问网页而非人工浏览,就一律构成 CFAA 刑事犯罪
尚不确定、仍在演变:hiQ 诉 LinkedIn 案倾向认定爬公开数据不必然违反 CFAA
判断标准其实很简单:只要爬取行为完全不以盈利为目的就一定合法,一旦沾上任何商业化使用就必然违法
options_en: Definitely legal: as long as a page is publicly accessible, anyone can scrape it freely, with no terms-of-service or legal constraint.
Definitely illegal: any automated program access to a page, as opposed to manual browsing, is automatically a CFAA crime.
Unsettled and evolving: the hiQ ruling leaned toward finding that scraping public data isn't necessarily a CFAA violation.
The rule is actually simple: scraping is always legal as long as it's not for profit, and always illegal the moment any commercial use is involved.
optionExplanations: 「绝对合法无限制」过度简化,爬取仍受 robots.txt、服务条款、地区法规约束。
「任何爬取都违法」同样错,判例恰恰表明公开数据爬取不必然构成 CFAA 违规。
对;hiQ 诉 LinkedIn 案给出「公开数据爬取不必然违反 CFAA」的参考,但整体法律仍未定,面试该谨慎表述。
盈利与否不是清晰的合法界线,现实由服务条款、判例、地区法综合决定,不是「沾商业就违法」这么绝对。
optionExplanations_en: 'Definitely legal, no limits' oversimplifies; scraping is still bound by robots.txt, terms of service, and regional law.
'Any scraping is illegal' is equally wrong; the case suggests public-data scraping isn't necessarily a CFAA violation.
Correct — the hiQ ruling leaned toward permitting public-data scraping under CFAA, but the law keeps shifting, so hedge your answer instead of stating an absolute.
Profit isn't a clean legality line; reality is decided by terms of service, case law, and regional statutes together, not an absolute 'any commercial use is illegal'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 美国计算机欺诈和滥用法,常被援引界定未授权访问;爬公开数据是否触发它尚有争议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CFAA (Computer Fraud and Abuse Act) is a US anti-hacking law often invoked for unauthorized access; whether scraping public data triggers it is contested.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一桩关于爬取 LinkedIn 公开资料的诉讼,判例倾向公开数据爬取不必然违反 CFAA。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: hiQ v. LinkedIn is a lawsuit over scraping public LinkedIn profiles, with rulings leaning that scraping public data isn't necessarily a CFAA violation.

scenario: 买来的第三方人口统计数据,可能编码了历史上的歧视性模式(如某地区历史信贷歧视)。
scenario_en: Purchased third-party demographic data may encode historical discriminatory patterns (e.g. a region's historical credit discrimination).
q: 外购人口数据可能带来什么风险,该怎么办?
q_en: What risk can purchased demographic data carry, and what should you do?
why: 它可能编码历史偏见,直接引入公平性风险:模型会把历史歧视当规律学下来、放大。必须做偏见/来源审计(bias & provenance auditing)——查数据从哪来、有没有系统性偏差,再决定用不用、怎么缓解。
why_en: It may encode historical bias, introducing a fairness risk as the model learns and amplifies past discrimination, so run bias and provenance auditing before using it.
options: 外购的人口统计数据天然中立客观,直接拿来训练即可,不需要额外做审计
它可能编码历史偏见→公平性风险;要做偏见/来源审计,查来源与系统性偏差再决定用不用
只要采购的数据量够大,统计上就能自动抵消掉里面可能存在的历史偏见
数据里是否存在历史偏见完全是卖数据的第三方数据商单方面的责任,买方使用时无需关心
options_en: Purchased demographic data is inherently neutral and objective; use it directly for training with no extra audit needed.
It may encode historical bias → fairness risk; run bias/provenance auditing to check source and systematic bias before deciding to use it.
As long as the purchased data volume is big enough, statistics will automatically cancel out any historical bias it might carry.
Whether the data carries historical bias is entirely the third-party broker's own responsibility; the buyer needn't worry about it when using it.
optionExplanations: 外购数据常携带采集环境的历史偏见,「天然中立直接用」会把歧视学进模型。
对;历史偏见是真实公平性风险,偏见/来源审计是使用外购数据前的必要防线。
数据量大只会放大而非抵消系统性偏见,量不能替代审计。
买方使用即担责,公平性后果落在你的系统上,不能把历史偏见的审查全推给数据商。
optionExplanations_en: Purchased data often carries the historical bias of its collection setting; 'inherently neutral, use directly' learns discrimination into the model.
Correct — historical bias is a real fairness risk, and bias/provenance auditing is the necessary safeguard before using purchased data.
More data amplifies rather than cancels systematic bias; volume can't replace an audit.
The buyer bears responsibility in use; fairness consequences land on your system, and you can't offload the historical-bias review entirely onto the broker.

termDefinitions.meaning: 追溯数据从哪来、怎么采的,评估其是否携带系统性偏差或合规问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Provenance auditing traces where data came from and how it was collected, assessing systematic bias or compliance issues.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据里编码的过去歧视性模式,模型若照学会放大不公平结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Historical bias is past discriminatory patterns encoded in data; a model that learns them amplifies unfair outcomes.

scenario: 面试官问「你会用什么数据?」,你要在 3 分钟内给一个有结构的 3 层回答。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'what data would you use?' and you give a structured 3-layer answer in under 3 minutes.
q: 把「你会用什么数据」的 3 层回答排成正确顺序:
q_en: Order the 3-layer 'what data would you use' answer correctly:
steps: 采集架构:事件驱动管线 + schema 强制 + 分区 + exactly-once
信号枚举与优先级:列隐/显式候选,按体量/噪声/相关性排序并说取舍
augmentation + 约束:外部数据补缺口,主动提 GDPR 最小化、偏见审计、consent
why: 3 层顺序:先枚举并优先级排序信号(用什么、为什么这个顺序)→ 再讲采集架构(怎么可靠地收)→ 最后讲外部增强与合规约束(补缺口 + 主动提 GDPR/偏见/consent)。从「用什么数据」到「怎么收」再到「合规兜底」,层层递进。
why_en: Enumerate and prioritize signals first, then the collection architecture, then augmentation and compliance constraints, moving from what data to how to collect it to how to stay compliant.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["1 信号枚举+优先级"] --> B["2 采集架构
事件驱动+schema+exactly-once"] B --> C["3 增强+合规约束
外部数据+GDPR+偏见审计"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 在收集/使用个人数据前取得用户明确许可,是 GDPR/CCPA 的核心要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consent is obtaining the user's explicit permission before collecting/using personal data, a core GDPR/CCPA requirement.

scenario: 两个团队,一个花大力气调模型架构却用着弱数据信号,另一个先把数据信号做扎实。
scenario_en: Two teams: one heavily tunes model architecture on weak data signals, the other first gets the data signals right.
q: 「信号→标签空间→目标函数→性能天花板」这条链意味着什么?
q_en: What does the 'signals → label space → objective → performance ceiling' chain imply?
why: 数据决定上限、架构只能逼近上限:你收集的信号决定标签空间,标签空间决定能优化的目标函数,目标函数决定性能天花板。架构调优补不了弱数据策略——天花板是数据钉死的,再好的模型也顶不破。
why_en: Data sets the ceiling and architecture only approaches it: collected signals fix the label space, which fixes the objective, which fixes the performance ceiling, so tuning can't compensate for weak data.
options: 架构才是真正的天花板,数据只要总量够多就行,单条信号的质量不重要
只要把模型参数量堆得足够大、训练算力堆得足够多,再弱的数据也能训出很强的模型,天花板可以忽略不计
信号、标签空间、目标函数三者相互独立,谁也不由谁决定、谁也决定不了谁
数据决定上限、架构只能逼近:信号定标签空间→定目标函数→定性能天花板,调架构补不了弱数据
options_en: Architecture is the real ceiling; data just needs enough total volume, and the quality of any single signal doesn't matter.
As long as the model's parameter count and training compute are both stacked big enough, even weak data can train a strong model, and the ceiling can be ignored.
Signals, label space, and objective function are mutually independent; none determines any of the others.
Data sets the ceiling and architecture only approaches it: signals fix the label space → objective → performance ceiling, and tuning can't fix weak data.
optionExplanations: 多不等于好——弱信号即使海量也把标签空间和目标函数框在低天花板,数据质量才是关键。
模型再大、算力再多也学不到数据里没有的信号,弱数据的天花板无法靠模型规模或算力突破。
三者恰恰是逐级决定关系:信号定标签、标签定目标,说互相独立否定了整条因果链。
对;这条链说明数据是上游地基,天花板由信号钉死,架构只能在天花板下逼近。
optionExplanations_en: Plentiful isn't good — weak signals, however massive, cap the label space and objective at a low ceiling; data quality is the key.
However big the model or however much compute you throw at it, it can't learn signals absent from the data, so weak data's ceiling can't be broken by scale or compute.
The three are exactly a cascade: signals fix labels, labels fix the objective; 'independent' denies the whole causal chain.
Correct — the chain shows data is the upstream foundation, the ceiling is fixed by signals, and architecture only approaches it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给定数据信号所能达到的最好表现上限,架构调优只能逼近而无法突破它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The performance ceiling is the best achievable given the data signals; tuning can approach but not break it.

scenario: 自检你有没有记牢信号丰富度层级和它的用途。
scenario_en: Self-check that you've locked in the signal richness hierarchy and its use.
q: 填空:信号丰富度层级与它指导的事。
q_en: Fill in: the signal richness hierarchy and what it guides.
text: 按意图强度:{{购买}} > {{点击}} > {{曝光}}。这个层级指导排序里 {{正/负标签}} 的分配——强意图行为当强正样本。
text_en: By intent strength: {{purchases}} > {{clicks}} > {{impressions}}. This hierarchy guides {{positive/negative label}} assignment in ranking, treating strong-intent actions as strong positives.
why: 购买>点击>曝光的意图梯度是分配正负标签的依据:购买是最强正意图、曝光最弱。记住它就能在排序题里合理定义标签。
why_en: The purchases > clicks > impressions intent gradient guides label assignment, with purchases the strongest positive and impressions the weakest.

scenario: YouTube 上不到 1% 的观看会被打显式评分,而几乎 100% 的观看都产生隐式行为信号。
scenario_en: On YouTube under 1% of views get an explicit rating, while nearly 100% generate implicit behavior signals.
q: 「显式评分覆盖率 <1%」这个事实对数据策略意味着什么?
q_en: What does the fact that 'explicit-rating coverage is <1%' imply for the data strategy?
why: <1% 是观测到的经验覆盖率(不是公式推导),它意味着显式信号太稀疏、无法单独支撑训练:必须以隐式信号做覆盖主力,把显式当稀有但可信的校准锚点。这个比例直接决定「隐式为主、显式校准」的融合策略。
why_en: The <1% is an observed empirical coverage, not a formula, and it means explicit signals are too sparse to train on alone, so implicit carries coverage while explicit serves as a rare-but-trustworthy calibration anchor.
options: 意味着应该只用那 <1% 的高质量显式评分来做训练,直接忽略掉隐式噪声
意味着显式太稀疏不能单撑训练:隐式做覆盖主力,显式当稀有但可信的校准锚点
意味着要想办法把评分率提到 100% 才能开始训练
意味着显式信号没用,应该完全放弃收集
options_en: It means you should only train on that under-1% of high-quality explicit ratings, directly ignoring implicit noise.
It means explicit is too sparse to train on alone: implicit carries coverage, explicit is a rare-but-trustworthy calibration anchor.
It means you must raise the rating rate to 100% before training can begin.
It means explicit signals are useless and collection should be dropped entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有某类信号的样本占比;显式评分 <1% 的覆盖率决定它只能校准不能单撑训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coverage rate is the fraction of items with a given signal; explicit ratings' <1% coverage means it can only calibrate, not train alone.

optionExplanations: 只用这不到 1% 的评分训练会把样本量砍到几乎可以忽略，等于扔掉了覆盖近乎全部用户的隐式行为。
对，这个比例说明显式只能是零星校准，训练的量级必须靠隐式撑起来。
把 <1% 当成故障去修就想反了——这是显式反馈天生的稀疏度，得绕着它设计，不是等它冲到 100%。
显式虽稀少，但它是干净、无歧义的校准锚点；扔掉它会让隐式噪声失去唯一的纠偏基准。
optionExplanations_en: Training only on that under-1% slice shrinks the dataset to almost nothing and throws away implicit behavior that covers nearly every user.
Right — that ratio locks in the strategy: implicit has to carry the bulk of training, explicit only spot-checks it.
Treating under-1% as a bug to fix gets the framing backwards — that sparsity is just how explicit feedback behaves, so design around it instead of chasing 100%.
Explicit signals stay valuable precisely because they're unambiguous; dropping them removes the only clean anchor for correcting implicit noise.
